Application of Gauss law: field of a charge sphere, line charge, charged plane conductor

card.title: Gauss law — flux counts the enclosed charge

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The field E = F/q₀ maps the force a charge WOULD feel at every point; field lines sketch it (out of +, into −, never crossing, density ∝ strength). Gauss law counts flux through any closed surface: total outward flux equals enclosed charge over ε₀ — shape-independent. With symmetric charge layouts, that one count hands you E with no integration.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: E = kQ/r² (point charge)  ·  Φ = ∮E·dA = Q_enclosed/ε₀  ·  plane sheet: E = σ/2ε₀ (single) · charged conductor surface: E = σ/ε₀  ·  line charge: E = λ/(2πε₀r)  ·  +4 μC at 2 m: E = 9×10⁹×4×10⁻⁶/4 = 9000 N/C

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Gauss law is always true; Gauss law is USEFUL only with symmetry (spherical, cylindrical, planar) so E factors out of the flux integral. Field-line sketches assume static charges. The conductor result (σ/ε₀ just outside) needs electrostatic equilibrium (charges at rest on the surface).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Two equal +2 μC charges 10 cm apart: midpoint fields are equal and opposite → E = 0 exactly (NEB 2020). Inside a charged spherical shell E = 0 (no enclosed charge); outside, the whole charge acts as if centred. Infinite sheet: uniform E, distance-independent.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: +4 μC point charge, field at 2 m: E = kQ/r² = 9×10⁹ × 4×10⁻⁶ / 4 = 9000 N/C radially outward (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Plane-sheet variant: choose a pillbox Gaussian surface straddling the sheet — flux 2EA (both faces), enclosed σA → E = σ/2ε₀ (NEB 2023, 5 marks).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Gauss gives total flux, not E point-by-point, without symmetry. Field lines are a map, not a mechanism — they begin/end only on charges (or infinity). The law is electrostatic; changing magnetic fields add induced E (Faraday) outside this unit.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Point charge flux: E·4πr² = (kQ/r²)·4πr² = Q/ε₀ — the r² cancels, so ANY enclosing surface passes the same flux (field-line counting made rigorous). Superpose for distributions: flux adds linearly → Φ = ΣQ/ε₀. Then invert for symmetric cases: sphere → E·4πr² = Q/ε₀; pillbox on sheet → E = σ/2ε₀.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: See 'infinite sheet/line/sphere' → Gaussian surface matching the symmetry (pillbox / coaxial cylinder / sphere), write flux = enclosed/ε₀, solve. Midpoint-between-equal-charges → zero by symmetry, no calculation. Lines never cross — use that to kill wrong MCQ sketches.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (5): Gauss law + field of an infinite plane sheet. NEB 2023 (3): +4 μC at 2 m numerical. NEB 2020 (3): twin +2 μC, 10 cm apart — midpoint field.
